findings.passage: Under current Ohio law, Ohioans wishing to own or use a short-barreled rifle, short-barreled shotgun or firearm suppressor must register those items with the federal government or face the risk of criminal prosecution. If that reflects the policy of this legislature, so be it. If, on the other hand, the legislature sees these registration requirements as archaic remnants of an overly restrictive past, it is time to eliminate them from Ohio law.
findings.note: Letter from the Attorney General to the Senate President and House Speaker, after the federal ATF stopped requiring NFA approval and registration of these items on Oct. 9, 2026. He lays out that Ohio law still ties legal possession to federal registration and says the legislature should drop those requirements if it sees them as outdated.
